chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Mansur ibn Hazim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the waiting period ('iddah) of the female slave who has not yet reached menstruation, while he was fearing for her, so he said: 'Five and forty nights.'

key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period ('iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a pre-pubescent female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the 'iddah for a pre-pubescent female slave as forty nights, diverging from the three menstrual cycles prescribed for free women. This ruling highlights the juristic distinction in Shia fiqh between free and enslaved women, where the absence of regular menstruation necessitates a fixed temporal period rather than a biological one, ensuring clarity in lineage and marital status.
